lines.text: Et claris fœcunda tulit uirtutibus olim,
lines.en: And formerly brought forth, fruitful in clear virtues,

lines.text: Teuthonis ora uiros,quos uirtus prodiga fummis
lines.en: The Teutonic shore, men whom lavish virtue

lines.text: Æquauit ducibus,prifcisq́ꝫ Heroibus illis.
lines.en: leaders, and to those ancient Heroes.

lines.text: Quos utinam noftro licuiffet tempore nafci,
lines.en: Would that it had been permitted for them to be born in our time,

lines.text: Aut nos illorum,quorum nos libera uirtus
lines.en: Or us in theirs, whose free virtue

lines.text: Ad facra templa poli ueheret, raperetq́ꝫ per auras
lines.en: might carry us to the sacred temples of the pole, and snatch us through the

lines.text: Ætherias,dignis meritis & honoribus auctos
lines.en: Ethereal, increased by worthy merits and honors.

lines.text: Effent qui rapidis penetrarent aëra pennis,
lines.en: There would be those who might penetrate the air with rapid wings,

lines.text: Et cœli ingenijs poffent tranfcendere nubes.
lines.en: And by their talents could transcend the clouds of heaven.

lines.text: Nec tam follicitè legeret mea Mufa patronum
lines.en: Nor would my Muse so anxiously choose a patron

lines.text: Te,Princeps Ernefte, paremq́ꝫ Heroibus ilis:
lines.en: You, Prince Ernest, and equal to those Heroes:

lines.text: Sed multi fimilesq́ꝫ tibi,fimilesq́ꝫ uetuftis
lines.en: But many similar to you, and similar to the ancient

lines.text: Spontè offerrentur proauis,qui noftra iuuarent,
lines.en: Forefathers would spontaneously be offered, who might help our

lines.text: Heu nimium contempta ifto ftudia aurea feclo.
lines.en: Alas, golden studies too much despised in this age.

lines.text: Effent,quos olim coleret non degener ætas,
lines.en: There would be those whom a not degenerate age might once cultivate,

lines.text: Atqꝫ inter cœli numeraret lumina:Sed nunc
lines.en: And number among the lights of heaven: But now

lines.text: Inuida nos pafsim reprimunt & triftia fata,
lines.en: Envious and sad fates repress us everywhere,

lines.text: Ferrea quæ nobis pepererunt fecula,ferro
lines.en: Which have brought forth iron ages for us, by the iron

lines.text: Armorumq́ꝫ ufu proftratis artibus, At tu
lines.en: And use of arms, with arts prostrated. But you

lines.text: Quæfo faue ftudijs his,Illuftrifsime Princeps,
lines.en: I pray, favor these studies, most Illustrious Prince,

lines.text: Ac mitis noftro precor afpirato labori.
lines.en: And gentle, I pray, breathe upon our labor.

lines.text: Hoc tua te uirtus monet,& generofa uoluntas,
lines.en: Your virtue advises you this, and your generous will,

lines.text: Et Patres Proauiq́ꝫ tui, clementia quorum
lines.en: And your Fathers and Ancestors, whose clemency

lines.text: In te nunc generis cum nobilitate reuixit,
lines.en: Has now revived in you with the nobility of your race,

lines.text: Ingenio cognata tuo,fanctę infita menti,
lines.en: Related to your talent, implanted in your holy mind,

lines.text: Quæ te fæpe facros Mufarum ducit ad amnes,
lines.en: Which often leads you to the sacred rivers of the Muses,

lines.text: Vraniæ dulcis cœleftia pocula libans.
lines.en: Pouring out the celestial cups of sweet Urania.

lines.text: Macte ifta uirtute tua, clarifsime Princeps,
lines.en: Be blessed in that virtue of yours, most clear Prince,

summary.headline: Dedication to Prince Ernest
summary.text: Dedicatory poem praising Prince Ernest, recalling the virtue of ancient heroes and lamenting the iron age’s neglect of the golden studies, while invoking the Muses and Urania.
